q: Does the paper's parallel-collision-finding scaling shape hold when we implement the actual deterministic-walk + distinguished-point + collector/verifier separation (rather than our brute-force partitioned linear scan), and does the empirically optimal architecture ratio (1/8 collectors, 1/4 verifiers, remainder workers) reproduce on modern CPU/GPU hardware?
basis: Our multiprocessing.Pool implementation reproduces the scaling shape via first-finder-wins over contiguous chunks; the paper's actual algorithm uses van Oorschot-Wiener DP-walks with distinct processor classes. We showed a shape match, not an algorithm match; the paper's Fig 4 (architecture-ratio optimum) is untested at any scale outside BG/Q.
next_steps: Build a Python (or Rust) reference DP-walk implementation with explicit collector/verifier processes over ZeroMQ or MPI4Py; sweep collector-fraction c in {1/16,1/8,1/4} and verifier-fraction v in {1/8,1/4,1/2} at N in {32,64,128} on a modern many-core box (e.g. uicgpu, spark-36ac); compare best-config wall time to first-finder-wins baseline; if the paper's ratio still wins, that's independent confirmation of Fig 4; if not, that's a real finding about how DP-walk overheads have shifted since 2016.

q: Can pQCS-style exact T-count synthesis be GPU-accelerated (unitary comparison in FP16/BF16 tensor cores + massive-batch DP-walk workers on a single A100/H100) to close the gap with a 4096-core BG/Q run on a single 8-GPU box?
basis: The paper's per-worker work is unitary multiplication + hashing, both trivially data-parallel and both extremely GPU-friendly at the small (8x8, 16x16) unitary sizes involved. No published pQCS variant runs on GPUs; the 2016 paper predates the GPU-for-symbolic-search wave.
next_steps: Port the DP-walk inner loop to CuPy or a JAX pmap on 4 or 8 A100s (uicgpu has 8, chicago-3 has similar); batch-evaluate 10^6 walks per GPU-launch; profile hash-collision overhead vs unitary-matmul overhead; benchmark against the paper's 26s-mean 4096-core Toffoli figure; publish speedup-per-dollar and speedup-per-watt vs BG/Q.

q: Does a hybrid classical/quantum synthesis pipeline (variational ansatz on IBM/IonQ hardware for the coarse decomposition, then pQCS for exact T-count-optimal refinement of Clifford+T sub-blocks) beat either endpoint alone on 5-8 qubit target unitaries?
basis: pQCS scales exponentially in circuit depth (paper Fig 6 shows the fraction-theta dependence at small problems); VQC/VQE hardware is noisy but samples from a much larger continuous ansatz space cheaply. A hybrid split has not been demonstrated for exact T-count-optimal synthesis.
next_steps: Take a 6-qubit target from a modern benchmark (e.g. a small chemistry unitary from qiskit-nature or a QFT variant); run a variational Clifford+T ansatz on a real IBM machine via qiskit-ibm-runtime to get a candidate decomposition D_coarse; run pQCS-style refinement on each Clifford+T sub-block of D_coarse; compare total T-count and wall time vs pQCS-only search from scratch. If hybrid wins on either metric, that motivates a full paper.

q: How does pQCS integrate with (and compare against) modern optimizing compilers -- specifically tket's TKET pass pipeline and Qiskit-transpiler's SABRE + collect2qBlocks + optimize1qGates at optimization_level=3, both of which now include T-count-aware passes derived from Amy/Nam post-pQCS-era work?
basis: pQCS was 2016; tket (Cambridge Quantum, 2019+) and modern qiskit-transpiler (post-2020) include many T-count reduction passes that were themselves informed by pQCS-era research. No head-to-head benchmark of pQCS vs current transpiler stacks on a common target set is published.
next_steps: Assemble 20 target circuits (10 named 3-4 qubit Toffoli variants + 10 from arithmetic benchmarks: adders, multipliers, comparators). Run tket's FullPeepholeOptimise + qiskit's optimization_level=3 vs pQCS (or a reference DP-walk implementation from Q2 above) on each. Tabulate final T-count and wall-time-to-optimum. If pQCS still wins on T-count, that motivates integrating pQCS as a tket/qiskit optimization pass; if it loses, that's a real finding about compiler-stack progress.

q: Can pQCS be extended to noise-aware synthesis -- picking a T-count-optimal decomposition among the (many) optimal solutions that minimizes expected error under a specific device noise model (T1/T2, gate infidelities, crosstalk) -- and does that materially reduce end-to-end circuit fidelity vs T-count-only optimization?
basis: pQCS finds a T-count-optimal decomposition but is agnostic to which optimal decomposition to pick. On real hardware, decompositions with the same T-count differ significantly in circuit depth, layout suitability, and crosstalk exposure. No noise-aware variant of pQCS is published.
next_steps: Enumerate all T-count-7 Toffoli decompositions (there are several tens known from the literature); simulate each under a realistic IBM Heron or IonQ Forte noise model using qiskit-aer + a device backend snapshot; identify which optimal decompositions have the highest expected process fidelity; formalize the noise-aware objective (T-count + weighted expected-error penalty) as a modification to the pQCS verifier stage; run on a small hardware allocation via IBM Quantum's open plan; publish 'noise-aware pQCS' if the fidelity gap exceeds 1 sigma of shot noise.
